newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel might be able to make Thomson bid.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel might be able to make Thomson bid.

text.p: Alcatel Alsthom chairman Serge Tchuruk told the National Assembly finance committee he would be open to making an offer for Thomson SA if the option were still there after December 31, according to minutes of the committee hearing released on Tuesday.

The government says it prefers a bid for state-owned Thomson SA by Lagardere, which has sparked controversy because of Lagardere's plans to hive off Thomson SA's Thomson Multimedia (TMM) unit to South Korea's Daewoo Electronics.
"Mr Serge Tchuruk reiterated that his group was bound by the bid which it had already made until the end of the validity of this offer on December 31," said the minutes.

"He also made it known that, if the matter was still open beyond December 31 and given the interest of an alliance with the Thomson group, Alcatel Alsthom could envisage a new offer which would take account of developments in the meantime and the current reactions," said the minutes.
In what looked like a new suggestion, the minutes reported Tchuruk as raising the possibility of the state opting for a sell-off of the entire Thomson group in phases.

"Based on the idea of a return to better times, he (Tchuruk) indicated that a step-by-step privatisation of the capital of the entire Thomson group could ultimately prove more profitable for the state than the current procedure of a sale in one go," he was quoted as saying.
Tchuruk highlighted that such a step could also address the issue of keeping Thomson intact, the minutes said.
"Among those reactions, the widening opposition to a pure and simple hiving off of Thomson Multimedia to a third party was understandable," the minutes reported Tchuruk as saying.
They said Tchuruk repeated that the offer made by Alcatel envisaged Alcatel holding onto 50 percent of TMM as well as playing a continued active role in its management.

Tchuruk, who did not elaborate on his group's intention to probably involve an Asian group in the offer, also told the committee his offer included a commitment to hand over to the state any capital gain made on an eventual opening of TMM's capital, the minutes said.
